title: Count of Range Sum
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<long long> prefix: n+1 entries → O(n)
- vector<long long> temp: n+1 entries → O(n)
- recursion call-stack depth: O(log n)
- not counted: input nums, returned int
approach: Rewrite each range sum S(i, j) as P[j+1] − P[i] where P is the prefix-sum array (P[0]=0). The task becomes counting index pairs (i, j) with i < j and lower ≤ P[j] − P[i] ≤ upper. Sort P with merge sort; during each merge, both halves are already sorted, so for every left-half element P[i] use two monotone pointers over the right half to count values in [P[i]+lower, P[i]+upper]. Summing these cross-pair counts with the recursively computed counts gives the answer in O(n log n).
hints: With n up to 10^5, there are roughly 5×10^9 pairs (i, j) - far too many to check directly. Can each range sum S(i, j) be rewritten as a difference of two values, each depending on only one index?

Use prefix sums P[k] = sum of nums[0..k-1], so S(i,j) = P[j+1] − P[i]; count pairs (i,j), i<j, with lower ≤ P[j]−P[i] ≤ upper via merge sort, using two pointers per merge. For nums=[−2,5,−1], prefix=[0,−2,3,2]; after sorting halves to [−2,0] and [2,3], the merge finds P=2 inside P[i]=0's window [−2,2], helping reach the total 3.

function count(lo, hi):
    if lo >= hi: return 0
    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
    count = count(lo, mid) + count(mid+1, hi)
    p = q = mid+1
    for i from lo to mid:
        while p <= hi and arr[p] < arr[i] + lower: p++
        while q <= hi and arr[q] <= arr[i] + upper: q++
        count += q - p
    merge arr[lo..mid] with arr[mid+1..hi] into temp, copy back
    return count

**Overflow** - prefix sums of values near 2^31−1 exceed 32 bits once n ≥ 2.
`Input: nums = [2147483647,2147483647,2147483647], lower = -5, upper = 5` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: storing prefix sums as `int` → prefix[2] wraps to −2, counted as in [−5,5], returns 2 instead of 0.

**All zeros** - every range sum equals 0, so every pair counts.
`Input: nums = [0,0,0], lower = 0, upper = 0` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: using `arr[p] <= l` instead of `<` in the lower-bound loop → skips equal elements, returns 0 instead of 6.

**Negatives with boundary ties** - the upper boundary itself must be included.
`Input: nums = [-1,-1], lower = -2, upper = -1` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: using `arr[q] < r` instead of `<=` in the upper-bound loop → excludes the upper boundary, returns 2 instead of 3.

**Single element** - only one range sum exists.
`Input: nums = [0], lower = 0, upper = 0` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: base case `if (lo >= hi) return 0;` written as `if (lo > hi) return 0;` → recurses forever / miscounts on length-1 prefix segments.

followUps.q: What if nums arrives element-by-element as a stream and you must report the running count after each new element?
followUps.a: Keep a sorted structure (balanced BST or Fenwick tree over compressed prefix-sum values) of all prefix sums seen so far. For each new prefix sum P[j], query how many previous P[i] lie in [P[j]−upper, P[j]−lower] in O(log n), then insert P[j]. Total O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

followUps.q: What if you must count range sums exactly equal to a single target k instead of a range?
followUps.a: Same merge-sort skeleton, but during each merge count right-half values equal to P[i]+k. Since both halves are sorted, use binary search (equal_range) to count duplicates of P[i]+k in the right half. Still O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

followUps.q: What if auxiliary memory is capped at O(1) beyond the input array?
followUps.a: Replace the O(n) temp buffer with an in-place merge sort; counting during an in-place merge costs O(n log n) per level, giving O(n log² n) time but O(log n) stack space only. You would store prefix sums back into a widened copy of the input if its type can hold them.
